question: Does maintaining the keyed VDOM global index from reconciliation attach/detach events reduce structural update time compared with rescanning the prior and updated keyed subtree after each keyed-region commit, under the same reconciler?

hypotheses.primary: Delta maintenance will lower per-page median update time than keyed-subtree rescanning for rotation, edge replacement, and each filter direction.
hypotheses.mechanism: Delta maintenance visits only inserted or removed mounted nodes for filter and edge replacement, and zero key-index nodes for a pure reorder; keyed-subtree rescanning revisits the whole target subtree before and after every update.
hypotheses.context: React is included as a contextual reference, not as the causal control for the index-maintenance hypothesis.

design.armOrder: Seeded shuffle of six arm permutations; permutation frequencies are balanced across 32 updates.
design.replicationUnit: Fresh visible browser page; update samples within a page are repeated measures, not independent replications.
design.browserProfile: One Chrome 154 MacIntel profile, one device, visible tab, 10 hardware threads, DPR 2; report actual environment from every page record.

measurements.primary: Per-page median paired difference (rebuild minus delta) and paired ratio (rebuild divided by delta) for measured updates, grouped by operation and explicit filter direction.
secondary: Per-page update p95 by arm and operation/direction.
One mount and one teardown duration per arm, per operation, per page; summarize across pages only.
Output parity, retained host identity, removal/reinsertion identity, and empty-container teardown contracts.

limitations: This is a mechanism-level host-reconciliation study, not a full application or component-state comparison.
Five page replications on one device cannot establish performance across browsers or hardware.
Mount and teardown have one timing observation per arm and scenario per page; they are descriptive.
The benchmark compares update-to-host-commit time and does not claim smoother frame presentation.
